title: From One Model Call to Authentic Coding AI

lines.title: Start with one prompt
lines.sub: Ten steps to an AI that reads, edits, and verifies code
lines.say: Welcome to Authentic Coding AI Academy. We will start with one model call, then build an AI that can read code, edit files, and run tests.
lines.cap: From one call to a complete coding AI

lines.title: Add one skill at a time
lines.sub: Learn, try, get feedback, then move forward
lines.say: Each lesson adds one skill. First understand it, then try it. After every run, the right panel shows what the program is doing.
Lesson one makes one model call. The program creates one user message, sends it, and prints the answer. There is no memory and no tool yet.
Run the lab. The right panel shows user input, model request, and model answer. The smallest input and output loop is now complete.
Lesson two adds message history. A model does not remember the last chat by itself. The program saves old messages and sends them again.
The system message holds the rules. User messages hold questions. Assistant messages hold earlier answers. Together they make a continuing chat.
Lesson three lets the model see code. The program reads useful files and adds their text to this request. The model sees only what the program sends.
Do not send the whole project. Search first, then choose useful files and code sections. Smaller, focused context usually gives a better answer.
Lesson four adds tools. A tool is an action the program allows. The model may ask to read a file, but the program performs the real action.
The model first sees each tool name, purpose, and input shape. After it chooses, the program checks the path, permission, and input before running anything.
lines.cap: The model asks; the program acts

lines.say: Lesson five joins the model and tools into a loop. Tool results return as messages. The model can choose another step or end the task.
Every loop needs an exit. We set a step limit and keep a cancel button. A bad plan cannot run forever.
Lesson six builds the file tool set. Search narrows the area. Read explains the code. Patch changes only the needed lines.
Order matters. Search first, read next, and edit last. Make small changes and show the user a clear diff.
Lesson seven adds the test loop. A model saying done is not proof. The program runs tests and reads the real output.
When a test fails, the error returns to the model. It makes a small fix and tests again. The task ends only after checks pass.
Lesson eight handles large projects. The program estimates input size, reads only useful code, and shortens older history into a summary.
A summary can be short, but key errors, diffs, and test proof must stay. They decide whether the next step is safe.
Lesson nine adds safety limits. File paths must stay inside the project. Commands use allowed tools and have time limits.
High-risk actions cannot run in secret. The program shows the impact and waits for a person. Safety wraps every tool call.
Lesson ten connects everything. The planner chooses a step. The executor runs a safe tool. The verifier checks the result with tests.
The full path is understand the task, search code, read files, make a small edit, run tests, then continue or stop from the result.
The final answer needs more than done. It shows what changed, which tests passed, and which risks still need a person.

lines.title: Authentic Coding AI
lines.say: This is authentic coding AI. It is not a chat program that only says it finished. It acts inside clear limits and proves the result with real evidence.
